newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil senate committee approves Brady bond bill.
newsitem.headline: Brazil senate committee approves Brady bond bill.

text.p: A committee in the Brazilian senate has approved a bill authorizing the Central Bank to buy back Brady bonds and swap them for other sovereign debt, the head of the committee said.
The version of the bill approved by the committee, which now goes to the floor of the Senate, sets no limit on the amount of debt the Central Bank may buy back, Sen. Gilberto Miranda said.
The draft bill, the product of an accord between committee members, was passed without debate and with a show of hands.
Government leaders were expected to push for a motion giving the bill priority status on the floor of the Senate, which could mean a final vote on the bill this week.
The bill would allow the Central Bank to restructure all its $57 billion in Bradies, should it decide to do so, but would set strict Senate oversight conditions.
The bank would have to report to the Senate 30 days after each operation or within 10 working days if operations totaled $500 million or more.
Failure by the Central Bank to report on time would mean automatic suspension of its authority to carry out further buybacks of debt swaps.
The bank would also have to satisfy senators that each operation had benefited the country, either by reducing its external debt stockpile, increasing maturities or improving the profile.
